gates.description: CPU Gate: interpreter identity challenge, structured per-tool reports, actual in-container uid, and a typed finalized artifact -- each read from evidence, not from an exit code. Exit 0 with nothing run is a FAIL.

Runs one device workload as root inside the container, on an explicitly named device, with the identity assertion executed in-payload. REFUSES to open a card another tenant already holds: occupancy is read first, before torch_npu or aclInit, and a held card yields 75 BLOCKED_ENV. TF_ALLOW_BUSY_DEVICE=1 is the deliberate, recorded override.

ordering.observedFailure: Without CANN sourced first: ImportError: libhccl.so: cannot open shared object file, from torch_npu/npu/utils.py importing torch_npu._C. With CANN sourced first: torch_npu 2.12.0 imports, exit 0. Both directions observed.
traps: set_env.sh breaks under set -u (expands unset LD_LIBRARY_PATH, PYTHONPATH, CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH)

busyDevicePolicy.default: REFUSE with exit 75 BLOCKED_ENV when another tenant holds the card
busyDevicePolicy.why: A device open at 13:46:26 was followed 32 s later by a host-wide docker exec stall, with the card already held by other tenants. A failed aclInit still opens the device node, so probing a held card is not a neutral act.
busyDevicePolicy.ordering: Occupancy is read in gate_device BEFORE torch_npu is imported and before aclInit is reachable, and tests/device_policy.py enforces that order from the AST. A runtime test of the refusal branch would pass even if occupancy were read after a device had already been opened.
busyDevicePolicy.override: TF_ALLOW_BUSY_DEVICE=1 -- loud banner, recorded as overriddenBusyDevice=true, result is a SHARED-card result with provisional timings
busyDevicePolicy.superseded: The previous default was the inverse: record occupancy, proceed, and refuse only when TF_REQUIRE_EXCLUSIVE=1. That made walking onto another tenant's card the normal path.
